tour.overview:
Some two and a half million years ago, a great volcano collapsed in on itself, leaving the Ngorongoro Crater, a caldera about 19 kilometres wide with walls some 600 metres high. Its floor of grasslands, swamps, forest and a soda lake supports one of the densest populations of large animals in Africa, including black rhinos. The Ngorongoro Conservation Area, where Maasai herders live alongside wildlife, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

This private day takes you into the crater with a professional driver-guide in a 4x4.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours from Arusha
• Start and end: your hotel in Arusha or Karatu
• Type: private safari with driver-guide and 4x4
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The crater rim viewpoint.
• The crater floor.
• Lake Magadi.
• The Ngoitokitok spring.

WHY THIS WORKS
Crater visits are limited to six hours on the floor; an early private start makes the most of that time.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, couples, photographers and anyone short of time.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
Combine with Tarangire or Lake Manyara, or choose our 4-day Serengeti and Ngorongoro safari.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The rim is cold in the early morning: bring a warm layer. Vehicles must leave the crater floor by 18:00.

days.name: The crater rim, the crater floor, Lake Magadi and the hippo pool
days.description:
What to expect: a full game drive in the Ngorongoro Crater, with a driver-guide, private 4x4, fees and lunch.

Your driver-guide collects you at about 6:00 in Arusha, or later in Karatu, and drives up through the forest of the crater highlands to the rim, where the whole caldera opens below you. You descend the steep road to the floor.

On the grasslands, herds of wildebeest, zebras and gazelles graze, watched by lions and spotted hyenas. Elephant bulls with long tusks wander through the Lerai fever-tree forest, buffaloes gather in the swamps and, with luck and patience, your guide finds black rhinos on the open plains. Flamingos tint the shallows of Lake Magadi pink, and golden jackals, ostriches and crowned cranes are common.

Lunch is a picnic by the Ngoitokitok spring, where hippos wallow in the pool; keep an eye on the black kites that swoop on picnics. After an afternoon game drive, you climb out of the crater and return to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
06:00 – Pick-up in Arusha.
09:00 – Crater rim viewpoint.
09:30 – Descent and game drive.
12:30 – Picnic at the hippo pool.
13:30 – Afternoon game drive.
15:30 – Climb out of the crater.
18:30 – Back in Arusha.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Eat your picnic inside the vehicle at the hippo pool to avoid the kites.
• A Maasai village visit can be added.

INCLUDED: private 4x4 and driver-guide, crater and conservation fees, picnic lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Maasai village fee, drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Will we see rhinos?
faq.answer: Often, but they are few and shy; sightings are never guaranteed.

faq.question: How long is the drive from Arusha?
faq.answer: About 3 hours each way; staying in Karatu shortens it.

faq.question: Is the vehicle private?
faq.answer: Yes, with a pop-up roof for viewing.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Child seats are available on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Yes, as it is entirely by vehicle.

faq.question: Can we combine it with another park?
faq.answer: Yes, with Tarangire or Lake Manyara on a 2-day trip.

faq.question: Do we need vaccinations?
faq.answer: Check with your doctor; malaria prevention is recommended.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Warm layers for the rim, neutral light clothes, a hat and sun protection.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year; the crater has resident wildlife.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary on safari in Tanzania: guides, drivers and camp staff appreciate a tip if you were happy with their service, but it is always your choice. Your guide can suggest typical amounts.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
